title: Reading Poems Slowly
text:
Poetry rewards readers who take their time. Unlike a news article, a poem often asks us to stop and reread a single line. Poets choose each word carefully, so a small change in vocabulary can alter the whole mood. Many students find that short poems are a good way to practise close reading.

Some poems use a clear narrative, while others focus on images, such as a river at night or an empty street. In both cases, the reader must look for connections between the images and the feelings they suggest. Keeping a reading journal helps students record their first impressions and compare them with later readings.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what does a poem often ask the reader to do?
options: Stop and reread a single line

questions.text: What does the second paragraph say a reading journal helps students do?
options: Record first impressions and compare them with later readings

questions.text: Why might a small change in vocabulary matter so much in a poem?
options: Each word is chosen carefully, so the mood can shift

questions.text: What can be inferred about a reader who finds images in a poem hard to interpret?
options: They should stop reading poetry altogether
They would benefit from looking for connections between images and feelings
They must have no interest in literature
They should only read poems with a clear narrative

vocabulary.definition: the feeling or atmosphere a text creates
a story or account of events
the first thoughts or feelings a reader has

paragraph_translations: A poesia recompensa os leitores que dedicam tempo a ela. Diferentemente de uma notícia, um poema muitas vezes nos convida a parar e reler um único verso. Os poetas escolhem cada palavra com cuidado, de modo que uma pequena mudança no vocabulário pode alterar todo o clima do texto. Muitos alunos descobrem que poemas curtos são uma boa forma de praticar a leitura atenta.

Alguns poemas apresentam uma narrativa clara, enquanto outros se concentram em imagens, como um rio à noite ou uma rua vazia. Em ambos os casos, o leitor precisa procurar conexões entre as imagens e os sentimentos que elas sugerem. Manter um diário de leitura ajuda os alunos a registrar suas primeiras impressões e a compará-las com leituras posteriores.
